faqs.question: What changes a framing quote?
faqs.answer: Compare quotes against the same drawing revision and member schedule. Ask which inspections and other project responsibilities remain separate and how revised drawings or concealed damage will be priced before extra work proceeds.

sections.title: Heritage Status, Significance and Original Timber
sections.summary: Age or an architectural style alone does not establish heritage protection. Check the property’s status and discuss the proposed work through the relevant planning and heritage pathway before changing significant fabric. Approval requirements depend on the place and the work; there is no universal permit or mandatory adviser rule that can be inferred from a timber repair description. Official guidance is linked in the FAQ below.
paragraphs: Heritage timber work brings together the significance of existing fabric, its condition and the building’s present use. A visible original window may have heritage value even when it needs careful repair for weathering or operation. Retention can include targeted repairs; it need not mean leaving every defect untouched.

sections.title: Original Profiles and Joinery Evidence for Repairs
sections.summary: Surviving profiles, joints, hardware and finish evidence help establish an appropriate detail. A traditional joint or particular species may be relevant, but the repair specification should follow the actual element and the agreed conservation approach. Do not assume every period building needs the same timber, connector or coating simply because its appearance is similar.
paragraphs: Profiles, surviving sections, old photographs, hardware and adjacent examples can all inform a repair or replacement detail. Recording these references before dismantling helps avoid a generic modern interpretation. Where a precise match is not possible, the proposed difference should be discussed openly with the project team and any relevant heritage adviser, not concealed by vague language.

For example, an adjacent intact sash may show a profile that a damaged window no longer reveals. Record it before removal, then agree whether the proposed detail should be repaired, replicated or referred for conservation advice.

sections.title: Conservation Advice and Carpentry Responsibilities
sections.summary: MEL ONE can discuss heritage timber carpentry against the recorded condition and agreed project information. The relevant authority decides formal approvals; heritage advisers and other responsible specialists address their own scopes. Ask what assessment, drawings, specifications and authorisations the proposed work needs before appointing the repair work.
paragraphs: Structural concerns, active water entry, glazing, suspect coatings and other old materials may need separate assessment and specialist arrangements. Include those responsibilities in the project brief. A carpentry discussion does not establish engineering, hazardous-material or approval authority, and preparation should not disturb unknown materials merely to obtain a photograph.

sections.title: Moisture Checks, Handover Records and Future Care
sections.summary: Timber does not fail in isolation. Flashing, drainage, glazing, paint, sealants, ventilation and adjacent masonry can all influence the service life of a repaired element. A restoration scope should identify these interfaces and the trades involved. This protects both the historic material that remains and the new timber introduced as part of a careful repair.
paragraphs: Keep photos, notes on retained and replaced elements, material or finish information, and a simple schedule for review. This record gives future owners or trades a clearer picture of what was repaired and why. Heritage stewardship is easier when maintenance is based on evidence rather than a cycle of reacting only after paint failure, water entry or decay becomes obvious.

sections.title: Condition Checks Before Timber Floor Restoration
sections.summary: Solid timber boards have timber through their thickness, but that does not promise an unlimited number of sandings or a fixed lifespan. Existing sanding, fixing position, damage, movement and the board profile affect what can be restored. Assess the actual floor before treating sanding and oiling as the solution; local repairs or a different finish approach may be needed.
paragraphs: Before selecting solid or engineered timber, understand slab or subfloor condition, flatness, moisture history, access, acoustic expectations and transitions to adjacent rooms. These factors affect preparation, installation method and long-term movement more than a showroom sample can reveal.

sections.title: Solid and Engineered Timber Floors for the Room
sections.summary: Engineered flooring combines a timber surface with a layered construction. Products differ in wear-layer thickness, installation method, finish and repair options. Price and suitability cannot be expressed as one percentage of solid flooring. Check the manufacturer’s information and the existing floor before assuming it can be sanded or installed directly over a particular slab.
paragraphs: A ground-floor slab does not automatically make engineered timber suitable, and an upper floor does not automatically favour solid timber. Moisture assessment, subfloor preparation, acoustic requirements, floor height and the selected system need to agree. For rooms with frequent water exposure, confirm the product’s stated application limits before choosing any floor covering.

A sunny living room, upper-level bedroom, entry, apartment and renovation over an existing slab place different demands on timber flooring. Consider traffic, pets, direct light, furniture, cleaning habits and the desired feel underfoot. The most suitable product is the one whose visual character, maintenance needs and installation conditions all match the room’s real use.

sections.title: Appearance, Movement and Floor-edge Details
sections.summary: Timber is a natural material and can show grain, tone and seasonal movement. Board direction, width, feature grade, finish sheen and transition details influence how that variation reads across a room. Discussing samples and laying patterns early helps clients choose a look they will value over time rather than expecting every board to be identical.
paragraphs: Flooring projects often become complicated at thresholds, fireplace surrounds, built-ins, stair nosings, skirtings and door clearances. These details deserve attention before the main field is installed. A clear plan for edges and transitions creates a more durable, finished result and prevents a small unresolved junction from holding up a larger room at the end.

sections.title: Flooring Handover and Ongoing Care
sections.summary: The right cleaning method, furniture protection, prompt attention to spills and sensible use of mats can help preserve a timber floor. sections.title: Defined Carpentry Jobs, Fixed Quotes and Hourly Rates
sections.summary: If you are searching for a carpenter hourly rate in Adelaide, first write down the task, location and result you need. Adjusting a sticking door, replacing exposed deck boards and repairing concealed framing involve different preparation and uncertainty. MEL ONE's actual rates and project prices are not supplied in this guide; request pricing for your scope. A headline hourly figure cannot tell you the total without the expected time, materials, other charges and boundaries of the work. State whether you want a repair, replacement or assessment before choosing between proposals.
paragraphs: A fixed quote and hourly arrangement answer different questions. A quoted amount needs a defined scope, quantities, inclusions, exclusions and stated assumptions. For hourly work, ask how time is recorded, which activities are chargeable and how progress and further authorisation will be discussed. Clarify whether procurement, travel, setup and return visits form part of that time or are separate items. Neither arrangement removes uncertainty in hidden timber. Agree how investigation and any later repair will be priced rather than assuming every job can receive an unconditional fixed price before assessment.

sections.title: Photo Estimates, Measurements and Opening-up
sections.summary: Photos can help explain a concern and support an initial discussion, but they cannot reveal every connection or concealed surface. A close image of a rotten sill may omit the adjoining frame, drainage problem or access needed to remove it. Ask which observations support an estimate, which assumptions remain and what inspection is needed before a written quote. Record the accessible areas assessed and whether opening up is included. Avoid treating a preliminary allowance as confirmation that the whole assembly is sound or that further work will be covered by the same amount.
paragraphs: The supplied photo shows a tape measure across exposed, deteriorated deck timber. Measurements can help record the extent of an opened area and the dimensions of visible members, giving an assessor a clearer starting point than a close-up alone. They do not establish which timber can remain or turn a photograph into a fixed repair price. A damaged deck board and deterioration in the supporting frame are different scope questions; ask what has been inspected and what remains concealed. Before opening more of the deck, agree which investigation is included, how findings will be recorded and who can authorise further work. Keep dated photos and measurements with the written scope, then request the proposed repair, price and timing changes for approval before additional work proceeds.

Opening a board, lining or joint can expose decay beyond the visible patch. That discovery can change the quantity of timber, connection details and specialist input needed. Ask how findings will be documented and which part of the original scope can proceed. MEL ONE confirms proposed scope changes and pricing for your approval before additional work proceeds. Record the agreed variation and any effect on timing. Where the damage affects load-bearing timber, resolve the required assessment and design responsibilities before treating it as a routine cosmetic repair.

sections.title: Materials, Access and Finishing Allowances
sections.summary: A carpentry quote in Adelaide should identify the elements to be repaired or supplied, with quantities or dimensions where practical. Describe the material, profile, grade or product selection rather than writing only 'new timber'. Confirm who orders, transports and stores it, and whether fittings, fasteners, protective coatings and delivery are included. Where you supply materials, discuss suitability, quantity and readiness before booking installation. Ask how unavailable products or requested substitutions will be handled. A material allowance needs a clear basis so a later selection can be compared with what was originally priced.
paragraphs: Work above a verandah, beneath a floor or around occupied rooms may need different access and protection arrangements. Identify restricted parking, stairs, working height, furniture, business hours and any coordination with other trades. Separate removal of old components from disposal, waste transport and final cleaning. State whether painting, staining, sealing, making good and adjoining surfaces are included, excluded or handled by another trade. For fascia, eaves or weatherboards, clarify the interfaces with gutters and surrounding materials. These details explain scope differences that a single total or hourly rate leaves hidden.

Suppose one proposal replaces selected deck boards while another allows for lifting a larger area and inspecting the joists. Their totals describe different work. Compare the measured area and board quantities, material specification, frame investigation, connections, stairs and balustrades. Then compare labour, procurement, access, removal, waste and finishing responsibilities. Ask both providers to identify retained components and unresolved findings against the same brief. An apparently lower price may cover fewer elements; a larger scope still needs explanation. Keep the comparison focused on what your deck needs rather than assuming either total proves better value.

sections.title: Checks Before Accepting a Written Quote
sections.summary: Read the quote as a complete document: agreed work, exclusions, allowances, GST treatment, payment stages, quote validity and proposed timing should be clear. Ask whether assessment, travel or a minimum booking charge applies; this guide does not assume those items are free or specify amounts. Note the acceptance process and who can approve changes, especially for rental or shared property. Send questions together so the revised written scope answers them before work starts. Keep the accepted quote and approved variations available for the final handover and account discussion.

Agree any opening-up allowance, document the findings and approve scope and price changes before additional work proceeds.

faqs.question: Does a carpentry quote include materials, rubbish removal, paint and GST?

Ask separately about deck boards and supports, stair components, pergola posts and overhead members. sections.title: Timber and Composite System Specifications

Ask the supplier or manufacturer to confirm the proposed supporting arrangement, fixing method and movement provisions for the selected product. paragraphs: Ask the proposed supplier to identify the timber species or product name, dimensions, grade, treatment where relevant and intended use. Keep the board surface separate from the structural timber specification. Request supporting product information and flag any gaps for review by the responsible designer or supplier. Compare samples for appearance and surface feel, but record what the order actually includes: profiles, edge details, colour selection and any coating. sections.title: Drainage, Ventilation, Framing and Fixings
sections.summary: WoodSolutions' domestic deck guidance identifies drainage and ventilation as design considerations. Raise questions about water leaving the surface, air moving beneath the deck and access for inspection. Proposed edge screens, landscaping and storage beneath the boards should be included in that discussion. Ask the designer to resolve ground clearance, board spacing and interfaces using the selected system's requirements. These details are especially useful when comparing a raised deck with a constrained, low-level area. A decorative finish cannot stand in for a workable drainage and ventilation arrangement.
paragraphs: For exposed coastal timber work, WoodSolutions' guidance gives particular attention to fixing selection. Ask which fasteners and connectors are proposed for the actual exposure, timber and supporting material, and what documentation supports that choice. sections.title: Finish and Maintenance in the Written Scope
sections.summary: Decide how you want the surface to look and what upkeep you can accommodate. Ask the coating supplier about preparation, compatibility with existing finishes, end-grain treatment and the process for later refinishing. For composite, obtain the selected manufacturer's cleaning and care instructions; ModWood provides separate care resources in its technical documentation. Keep a record of the installed product and any finish so future cleaning or repair can follow the relevant guidance. paragraphs: A useful brief names the intended use, observed exposure, proposed boards, supports, fixings, finish and maintenance expectations, then identifies decisions still awaiting assessment. For restoration, ask which sound components could remain and what would be inspected before reuse. For a new outdoor structure, resolve drawings and responsibility for connections first. faqs.question: Can I identify the timber specification or compliance from an outdoor project photo?

Ask for the material specifications, relevant product and design documents, and any required approval records. Keep finish and care instructions with the handover information for each component.

faqs.question: Which timber and fixings suit an exposed coastal deck?
faqs.answer: Start with the actual exposure and the whole assembly. Ask the supplier or responsible designer to specify boards, supports, fasteners and connectors together, with evidence for the proposed application. Record corrosion and moisture concerns for assessment. A species name or suburb alone is not a complete specification.

faqs.question: Can I replace timber boards with composite on the existing frame?
faqs.answer: Have the frame assessed and compare it with the exact product's installation requirements before assuming it can be retained. Request confirmation of supports, fixings and movement details. The selected manufacturer's instructions should guide that review; one composite product's instructions do not establish suitability for another.

faqs.question: Why can two decks need different materials and maintenance plans?
faqs.answer: Their exposure, drainage, ventilation, supporting arrangements and use may differ. Record those conditions and ask for a care plan tied to the selected boards and finish. Obtain the relevant product documents rather than assuming a universal service life, maintenance interval or warranty outcome.

related_links.label: Example manufacturer resource: ModWood technical and care documents

faqs.question: Can bushfire-related requirements affect external timber work?
faqs.answer: Ask the relevant authority or responsible professional to assess the requirements that apply to the address and proposed work before choosing materials. This guide does not assign a bushfire rating, confirm product compliance or determine whether approval is required. Identify unresolved requirements in the project brief before ordering.

faqs.question: What does custom cabinetry cost?
faqs.answer: Cabinet dimensions, layout, door finish, internal fittings, hardware, removal and installation access affect the quote. faqs.question: How is decking priced?
faqs.answer: A deck quote depends on whether the work is a new structure or repair, the accessible frame condition, area, height, timber and finish, access and removal needs. Compare quotes for the same quantities, materials, labour, supply or collection, access, removal, waste, finishing and GST treatment. faqs.question: Does peeling fascia paint mean the whole board needs replacing?
faqs.answer: Peeling paint alone does not establish the repair extent. MEL ONE checks timber condition, board ends, joints, fixings and the adjoining base before comparing local repair, section replacement and full-board replacement. Painting and timber replacement are specified separately, so the quote explains both the repair and the intended finish.

faqs.question: Can one damaged weatherboard be replaced?
faqs.answer: Yes, MEL ONE provides single-board and multiple-board local replacement. The workable repair extent depends on adjoining timber, fixing positions, board profile and nearby trims. An onsite assessment establishes whether an individual board repair is suitable or whether a local group needs replacement to form the agreed junctions.

faqs.question: Does a squeaky or bouncing floor mean the joists need replacing?
faqs.answer: No single symptom establishes that conclusion. Floorboards, fixings, supporting members and connections can produce different movement or noise problems. MEL ONE inspects the safely accessible area to distinguish those possibilities and defines any further professional assessment before confirming local strengthening, replacement or a connection repair.

faqs.question: Is lowering a timber threshold enough to improve an entrance?
faqs.answer: It may be one part of the work, but the person's movement needs, entrance height, door swing, doorway width, landing and ground conditions must be considered together. MEL ONE assesses the proposed timber adjustment and adjoining junctions before confirming the scope. A formal accessibility outcome needs the relevant assessment and specified design rather than an assumption based on threshold height alone.

faqs.question: Can just one rotten pergola post be replaced?
faqs.answer: A single-post replacement may be suitable after the remaining timber, connections and supports are assessed. For a load-bearing member, confirm the design, temporary support, sequence and necessary approval arrangements before removal. A leaning structure should not be treated as a simple decorative replacement.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a stair tread and a stringer?
faqs.answer: A tread is the walking surface; a stringer supports the steps along the stair. Damage to a stringer is not covered simply by replacing a tread and should be assessed as a structural concern.

faqs.question: Can damaged cabinet hinge holes be repaired?
faqs.answer: Some local fixing areas can be repaired when sufficient suitable material remains. Swollen board or extensive damage around the hinge may require a separately scoped board repair or replacement; a new hinge alone may not resolve it.

about.story: MEL ONE supports homeowners, property managers, builders and businesses across Adelaide with on-site carpentry, workshop joinery, cabinetry, timber repair and maintenance. We begin with the condition of the property and the practical outcome the client needs: a safer deck, a workable kitchen, a repaired opening, a durable fitout or a well-resolved custom timber feature. That gives the project a clearer scope, helps coordinate the right trades and reduces avoidable surprises after work has started. Our approach is straightforward: explain what is known, identify what still needs checking, document the agreed work and keep communication practical as the job progresses.
